H1.quote: R-3 | Check-out and check-in work offline and sync when the phone is back online. ... Many pitches have no mobile signal at all.

H2.quote: No third-party cloud: data stays on club hardware. / GDPR applies to coach names and phone numbers.

H3.quote: The tool runs on the club's existing Synology NAS, in Docker. / Running cost: 0 EUR per month.

H4.quote: R-7 | The kit manager gets an overdue report by e-mail every Monday morning.

H5.quote: R-2 | Checking out an item takes at most 3 taps and under 15 seconds, by scanning a QR code on the kit bag. | Many volunteers are not tech-savvy

H6.quote: R-8 | A yearly inventory CSV export, for the treasurer and the insurance audit.

H7.quote: Ruled out: Performance efficiency (time behaviour and capacity). Reason: the scale is small (about 300 items, 40 coaches), and the architect says performance is not a concern.

H8.quote: One volunteer maintains it, and it must be handed over to the next maintainer. That volunteer knows Python only.

H9.quote: Lost-item history is kept for 2 years (insurance).

H10.quote: warn the kit manager 30 days before a first-aid bag item expires. Only first-aid bag items have expiry dates. (02-expiry-warning.md)

H11.quote: Out of scope: Money handling: deposits, fines, payments.

H12.quote: It must be live by 1 March, the start of the season.

unasked_decisions: QS-5 measure '0 of 20 test requests by non-manager accounts return a phone number': the architect only said QG-5 follows Q14 and never set the number 20
QS-4 adds '0 unreadable stores' beyond the confirmed candidate measure
The treasurer 'passes it to the insurer' / 'The insurer receives the CSV via the treasurer': the architect said who sends it on is up to the treasurer
Context lists the club's mail provider as an external system 'if the report is sent through it', although the architect asked for sending from the NAS
contradictions: ADR 0001 lists the crosscutting convention 'units (dates and currency)'; a currency convention implies money data, which conflicts mildly with the no-money-handling anti-goal (H11)
extras: Offline conflict handling: keep both events in time order and flag the item for the kit manager
Overdue defined as 7 days after check-out
Only the kit manager sees phone numbers; the phone number is deleted when a coach leaves
Edit permission model (R-6): any coach adds, only the kit manager corrects or deletes
Crash survival with no loss of synced check-outs (R-5, QS-4 kill-during-write trials)
Risks recorded for mail delivery vs no-third-party-cloud, unknown NAS backups, single maintainer and hard date
Quality scenarios QS-1..QS-5 with measurable responses
ADR 0001 lists centrally decided items, including the sync protocol versioning
